record.notes: First reading in the House of Commons on 10 June 2026 (sitting 133). LEGISinfo lists the bill as at second reading in the House of Commons, with no second-reading activity, no recorded votes and no major speeches. The Digital Safety Commission would set details of the obligations by regulation, including age estimation and verification and design features such as labelling tools; for social media services the government intends a minimum age of 16 for accounts. The bill was informed by the Expert Advisory Group on Online Safety, reconvened from March to May 2026.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: LEGISinfo's page for C-34 (45-1), stored 11 Oct 2026 and found unchanged by the archiver on 17 Oct 2026, confirms the long and short titles, the sponsor, the bill type, first reading on 10 June 2026 and the current status 'At second reading in the House of Commons' with no second-reading activity; the 45th Parliament, 1st session, runs 'to present'. Canadian Heritage's page on the bill (secondary source, page date 2026-09-08, also unchanged) confirms the duties of AI chatbot and social media services, the labelling of synthetically generated content and the deepfake provisions.

summary.quote: AI chatbot services will also be subject to a Duty to Act Responsibly, tailored to chatbot services, which will require them to: (1) mitigate the risk of the chatbot communicating harmful content; (2) implement emergency measures in crisis situations
(3) mitigate the risk that the chatbot will engage in harmful behaviour.
applying labels to synthetically generated content
intimate content communicated without consent including deepfake sexual images
